note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question a, wording: The stem says the trays make each batch 'waste less', which almost restates 'uses fewer materials'. The clue ('using less, or using something again?') narrows it further, so a student can pick Reduce without understanding the method. This is very easy for Year 12.

rejected.title: Waste minimisation
card: Waste minimisation means cutting the material a business throws away when it makes goods. It lowers costs, because less is paid for material that is never sold, and it harms the environment less, because less waste goes to landfill.
Reduce
use fewer materials in the first place, for example by cutting shapes more carefully from a sheet of fabric.
Reuse
use a material or item again for the same job or a new one, for example by refilling the same crate or container.
Recycle
turn waste into new material, for example by melting scrap metal to make new metal parts. Less new material is bought, and less is thrown out.
rejected.remember: Reduce, reuse or recycle: each saves money and spares the environment.

a.q: A bakery in Ballarat changes its trays so each batch of dough wastes less. Which waste minimisation method is this?
opts: Reduce, as it uses fewer materials
Reuse, as it uses the dough again
Recycle, as it makes new material
Reduce, as it sells the waste to others
a.why: Using less dough for each batch means fewer materials are used in the first place, which is reducing. Reuse would mean using the same item again, and the bakery is not doing that.
a.clue: Is the bakery using less, or using something again?

b.q: Priya runs a Geelong furniture workshop. She melts leftover aluminium offcuts and casts them into new table legs. What are the main effects of this?
opts: It cuts material costs and sends less waste to landfill
It raises material costs but sends less waste to landfill
It cuts material costs but sends more waste to landfill
It has no effect on costs but sends less waste to landfill
b.why: This is recycling, because waste is turned into new material. Priya buys less new aluminium, so costs fall, and the offcuts are no longer thrown out, so less goes to landfill. It is tempting to see recycling as only an environmental gain, but buying less new metal saves money too.
b.clue: Think about what Priya no longer has to buy or throw out.

draft.title: Waste minimisation
card: Waste minimisation means cutting the amount of material a business throws away when it makes goods. Waste is a cost, because the business paid for materials it did not sell.
Reduce
use fewer materials in the first place, for example by cutting shapes more carefully from a sheet of fabric.
Reuse
use a material or item again for the same job or a new one, for example by refilling the same crate or container.
Recycle
turn waste into new material, for example by melting scrap metal to make new metal parts.
draft.remember: Less waste means lower costs and less harm to the environment.

a.q: A bakery in Ballarat changes its trays so each batch of dough wastes less. Which waste minimisation method is this?
opts: Reduce, as it uses fewer materials
Reuse, as it uses the dough again
Recycle, as it makes new material
Reduce, as it sells the waste to others
a.why: Using less dough for each batch means fewer materials are used in the first place, which is reducing. Reuse would mean using the same item again, and the bakery is not doing that.
a.clue: Is the bakery using less, or using something again?

b.q: Priya runs a Geelong furniture workshop. She melts leftover aluminium offcuts and casts them into new table legs. What is the main way this helps her business?
opts: It cuts material costs and reduces landfill
It raises material costs but reduces landfill
It cuts material costs but adds to landfill
It avoids using any materials in production
b.why: This is recycling, because waste is turned into new material. Priya buys less new aluminium, so costs fall, and less waste goes to landfill. It does not remove the need for materials, as the metal is still used.
b.clue: Think about what Priya no longer has to buy or throw out.

a.best: Reduce, as it uses fewer materials

b.best: It cuts material costs and reduces landfill

problems.detail: The card explains only the cost benefit of waste minimisation. It never mentions the environmental benefit (less harm, less landfill), yet the point, the remember line and question b all rely on it.

The right option depends on knowing that recycling reduces landfill, which the card does not teach. Also, reducing landfill is an environmental benefit rather than a way it 'helps her business', so the stem fits the options loosely.

check.summary: The answers are sound. The card leaves out the environmental benefit of waste minimisation, so question b and the remember line rely on landfill and environmental harm, which the card never teaches.

a.q: A juice maker in Mildura collects the glass bottles it sells, washes them and fills them again with new juice. Which waste minimisation method is this?
opts: Reuse, as the same bottles do the same job again
Reduce, as fewer bottles are used in each batch
Recycle, as the glass is turned into new material
Reduce, as the bottles are washed before filling
a.why: The bottles are not broken down or made into anything new. The same item goes back into use for the same job, which is reusing. Recycling is the tempting choice, but it means turning waste into new material, and the glass here stays as it is.
a.clue: Does the bottle stay a bottle, or is it made into something new?
